title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: braised lamb mince under mashed potato
excerpt: Shepherd's pie is a British classic of spiced lamb mince in rich gravy, topped with a thick layer of mashed potato and baked until golden. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie has been a British staple since the late eighteenth century, originally made with leftover roast lamb. The name distinguishes it from cottage pie, which uses beef.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled and uncooked for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge before baking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the baking time if cooking from cold.

glossaryTerms.definition: A British baked dish of lamb mince topped with mashed potato.
A base of diced onion, carrot and celery cooked in fat to build flavour.

content.text: is one of the most comforting dishes in British cooking. The filling is a slow-cooked lamb mince built on a
of onion, carrot and celery, thickened with the braising liquid until it coats the meat in a rich gravy.

The mashed potato topping should be well seasoned and spread thickly. Use a fork to rake the surface into ridges; they catch and brown in the oven, giving every spoonful a mix of soft interior and crisp edges.
Heat a little oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb mince in batches, breaking it up as it cooks. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 more minutes.
Return the mince to the pan. Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and coats the meat.
While the filling cooks, boil the potato until completely tender. Drain well and mash with the butter and cream until smooth. Season well.
Spoon the filling into the baking tin. Spread the mash over the top and rake the surface with a fork. Bake at 200°C for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

attrs.problem: The mash sinks into the filling.
attrs.solution: Make sure the filling has cooled slightly before spreading the mash on top. Warm filling causes the mash to melt through.
Simmer uncovered for longer before topping. The liquid should reduce to a thick, glossy sauce before going into the oven.

attrs.problem: The mashed potato topping does not brown.
attrs.solution: Brush the surface with a little melted butter or push the tin to the top shelf. A brief blast under the grill at the end also works.

content.text: Shepherd's pie is a staple of British home cooking and pub menus across England, Wales and Scotland. It is weeknight food, eaten in winter when a warm oven is welcome. Pubs serve it year-round with a side of peas or green beans. It is one of the first dishes British children learn to make.
